name: RT-2 (Vision-Language-Action Models) — Technical Summary
observations: Source: PDF "RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control", Brohan et al., Google DeepMind, arXiv:2307.15818v1 (28 Jul 2023), 26 pages. Read from pdf/embodied_ai_papers on 2026-11-01 (pages 1-12 + appendix B/D).

Core idea (VLA): take an existing pretrained vision-language model (PaLI-X 5B/55B, PaLM-E 12B) and co-fine-tune it to emit robot actions directly as text tokens in the SAME output space as language. No new action-only layers or new parameters are added — model weights are fully shared between language and action tasks. Contrasts with using VLMs only as high-level planners feeding separate low-level controllers.

Action encoding: 8 integers per control step, string = 'terminate Δpos_x Δpos_y Δpos_z Δrot_x Δrot_y Δrot_z gripper_extension'. Space is 6-DoF end-effector positional+rotational displacement, gripper extension, and a terminate command. Continuous dims are discretized into 256 uniform bins and expressed as bin ordinals.

Action tokenization: PaLI-X already has a unique token per integer up to 1000, so bins map to the matching integer token. PaLM-E has no such scheme, so the 256 least-frequently-used tokens are overwritten to form the action vocabulary (a form of symbol tuning, Wei et al. 2023).

Training data format: inputs are robot camera image + instruction in VQA format ('Q: what action should the robot take to [instruction]? A:'), target is the numeric action string. Robot data = RT-1 dataset: 13 robots, 17 months, office-kitchen, 7 skills (pick, move near, place upright, knock over, open/close drawer, place into receptacle, pick from receptacle).

Key recipe = CO-FINE-TUNING, not plain fine-tuning: robot trajectories are mixed with the original web-scale VLM data (WebLI ~10B image-text pairs / 109 languages, filtered to ~1B examples, plus VQA/captioning). Robot data up-weighted to ~50% of each batch. Ablation shows robot-only fine-tuning generalizes worse, and training from scratch performs very poorly even at 5B.
Output constraint: during decoding for robot prompts, sampling is restricted to valid action tokens only; on standard vision-language prompts the full natural-language vocabulary remains available.

Real-time inference: models are served in a multi-TPU cloud service and queried over the network, allowing multiple robots to share one service. 55B RT-2-PaLI-X runs at 1-3 Hz; the 5B variant at ~5 Hz. Largest model used for direct closed-loop control at the time by over an order of magnitude.

Results: ~6,000 real-robot evaluation trials on a 7-DoF mobile manipulator. On seen tasks RT-2 is comparable to RT-1; on unseen objects/backgrounds/environments it is ~2x better than RT-1 and MOO and ~6x better than other baselines (VC-1, R3M). Also 90% on simulated Language-Table with a 3B PaLI vs 72-77% for BC-Zero/RT-1/LAVA.

Emergent capabilities transferred from web pretraining: symbol understanding ('move apple to 3', 'push coke can on top of heart'), visual/math/multilingual reasoning ('move apple to cup with same color', 'move X near the sum of two plus one', 'mueve la manzana al vaso verde'), and human recognition ('move the coke can to the person with glasses'). Best model >3x average success over the next-best baseline.

Chain-of-thought variant: a few hundred extra gradient steps on data augmented with an explicit 'Plan: <natural language> Action: <tokens>' step lets RT-2 do multi-stage semantic reasoning (pick a rock as an improvised hammer; pick an energy drink for someone who is tired). Bridges VQA data and manipulation data.
Scaling findings: larger models generalize better (5B vs 55B compared directly); co-fine-tuning beats robot-only fine-tuning at every size; from-scratch training is a dead end.

Stated limitations: the model gains no new physical skills — motor repertoire is still bounded by the robot data distribution (only the deployment of those skills improves); computation cost is high and inference frequency is a bottleneck for high-rate control (quantization/distillation suggested); very few openly fine-tunable VLMs existed at the time.

name: VLA Robotics Tooling Stack (2026 practice lookup)
observations: Looked up current best-practice open-source APIs for vision-language robotics workflows on 2026-11-01 via Context7 library resolution. Two relevant, well-maintained options were confirmed; an 'openvla' lookup returned only irrelevant matches (OpenClaw/OpenLayers/OpenBLAS) and was discarded as unresolved.

HuggingFace LeRobot (library ID /huggingface/lerobot, v0.6.1, ~4.5k code snippets, High reputation): end-to-end robot learning framework with a standard LeRobotDataset format on the Hub, `lerobot-train` (e.g. --policy.type=smolvla --policy.load_vlm_weights=true, --dataset.repo_id, --env.type=libero_plus, --steps/--batch_size/--env_eval_freq), and `lerobot-rollout` for deployment (--policy.path=user/policy, --robot.type=so101_follower, --robot.port, --robot.cameras='{front: {type: opencv, ...}}', --task, --duration).

LeRobot Real-Time Chunking (RTC) is the direct answer to RT-2's inference-latency limitation: `--inference.type=rtc --inference.rtc.execution_horizon=10 --inference.rtc.max_guidance_weight=10.0`, recommended for large slow VLA models (Pi0, Pi0.5, SmolVLA) to keep motion smooth despite high latency. Rollout also has a 'sentry' mode that records and auto-uploads every N episodes to an eval dataset repo.

Physical Intelligence OpenPI (library ID /physical-intelligence/openpi, High reputation): open checkpoints and packages for flow-matching VLAs (pi0, pi0.5), e.g. pi0_droid, pi05_droid, pi05_libero. Inference uses a policy server pattern: `uv run scripts/serve_policy.py policy:checkpoint --policy.config=pi05_libero --policy.dir=<ckpt dir>` which listens on port 8000 and is queried remotely by the robot runtime / eval script — closely analogous to RT-2's multi-TPU cloud serving design.

OpenPI fine-tuning API: a `TrainConfig` combines a model config (e.g. pi0.Pi0Config()), a LeRobot data config (LeRobotUR5DataConfig with repo_id, AssetsConfig pointing at base-checkpoint norm stats for cross-embodiment transfer, DataConfig(prompt_from_task=True) to read the instruction from the dataset's `task` field), and CheckpointWeightLoader('gs://openpi-assets/checkpoints/pi0_base/params'); typical runs are ~30k steps.

How the modern stack maps onto RT-2's ideas: (1) RT-2's network-queryable cloud inference service -> OpenPI policy server or LeRobot rollout; (2) RT-2's 256-bin text-token action decoding -> largely superseded by continuous/flow-matching action heads (pi0/pi0.5) and compact VLMs (SmolVLA); (3) RT-2's co-fine-tuning with web VLM data -> LeRobot's load_vlm_weights=true plus keeping VLM pretraining in the mixture rather than robot-only fine-tuning; (4) LeRobotDataset is the de-facto interchange format shared by both tools.
